title: RAW_UNSCREENED: ychor als Eintragsfortsetzung oder Rezeptimperativ
summary: RAW_UNSCREENED: ychor steht 13/13 am Zeilenanfang, nie am Absatzanfang; dieselben Folgefelder können einen weiteren Eintrag oder einen Arbeitsbefehl eröffnen.

design.scope_description: Exposed ychor lines and their cached complete line bodies in GDT756; no image or new corpus.
design.mechanism: Metatextual continuation marker: ychor introduces another item/entry; rival treats it as an imperative Recipe/Accipe.
design.unit: Exact ychor loci and first three complete body slots.
design.prediction: Continuation predicts ychor bodies remain item-like records and recur with heterogeneous content/amount/process fields without requiring an action host; imperative predicts a stable action-bearing body with an explicit patient/result.
concrete_observations: GDT756 reports 13/13 line-initial and 0/13 paragraph-initial ychor occurrences across four sections.
Examples f6v.8, f17v.15, f45v.9 and f102v2.35 have differing following content, quantity and process-like slots.
linked_consequences: A continuation reading predicts the same opener can precede descriptive and prescriptive records.
An imperative reading predicts a common written operand and resulting state in each selected body; missing operands remain failures, not invisible repairs.
design.nearest_rival: Recipe/Accipe imperative with a line-initial action frame.
design.distinguishing_observation: Predeclare body fields and count whether ychor lines contain a written action operand plus result versus merely a new item/record body; line position alone is not sufficient.
assumption_costs: ychor is a whole metatextual form
body slots can be typed without translating them
no paragraph boundary is inferred from line onset
design.strongest_likely_failure: The same mixed bodies can be rendered under both entry and imperative syntax, leaving no independent operand/result distinction.
